articles.title: Trump's Justice dept steps into US midterm battles before votes are counted, breaks decades-old practice
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump's Justice Department has stepped into election disputes ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections, breaking with decades of
articles.body: US President Donald Trump's Justice Department has stepped into election disputes ahead of Tuesday's US midterm elections, breaking with decades of practice aimed at keeping federal law enforcement agencies from appearing to favour a political party or candidate.The department has filed lawsuits challenging election procedures in California and Alaska, raising concerns among critics that its powers are being used to influence contests that could determine control of Congress and several governors' offices, Reuters reported.In California, the Justice Department sought to block mail-in ballots from around 20,000 voters it suspects may be non-US citizens and therefore ineligible to vote. It has also demanded election records as part of a related criminal investigation.California officials have rejected the move, saying the state has safeguards to prevent noncitizens from voting and arguing that the federal government lacks the authority to block the ballots.In Alaska, the department has stepped up a criminal investigation into whether a Senate candidate sharing the name of Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan entered the race to confuse voters. It also moved to prevent certification of the election result if Sullivan narrowly loses.However, a federal judge dismissed the department's lawsuit on Sunday, ruling against its attempt to intervene in the state's election process. The Justice Department has appealed the decision.According to Reuters, courts have now rejected the department's lawsuits involving both California and Alaska. The cases have highlighted the Trump administration's willingness to intervene in election disputes before ballots are counted and results are certified.Critics have warned that such moves could give Trump an opportunity to question the legitimacy of the midterm results."It appears that the administration wants the department to have an impact that was previously prohibited," Mark Blumberg, who formerly led the Justice Department's election response to civil rights threats, was quoted as saying by Reuters. He has since founded the Rule of Law Project.Attorney General Todd Blanche has defended the department's actions, saying they are lawful and intended to protect election integrity."The Department isn't helping any campaign. It's enforcing the law," Justice Department spokesperson Kiersten Pels said.Trump's claims of voter fraudUnder the US Constitution, individual states are responsible for administering elections. However, Trump has repeatedly accused Democratic-led states of failing to prevent noncitizens from voting, although voting by non-US citizens is already prohibited under federal law.Trump has also continued to make false claims that widespread voter fraud cost him the 2020 presidential election. Independent investigations and state audits have found that voter fraud is rare.During his first term, Justice Department officials resisted pressure to intervene in efforts to challenge Trump's 2020 election defeat. Outside groups aligned with the Republican leader subsequently filed more than 60 lawsuits disputing the results, but none succeeded.Lis Frost, a voting rights lawyer with Elias Law Group, which frequently represents Democrats in court, said the situation had changed."The right-wing fringe outside groups are not going to have to do that this year because the DOJ is clearly standing ready and willing to do it," Frost told Reuters.Traditionally, the Justice Department's election-related interventions have focused on enforcing federal laws that protect the voting rights of racial minorities and other vulnerable groups.Alaska election becomes legal battlegroundAlaska has emerged as a major focus of the dispute following a New York Times report that Democratic candidate Mary Peltola's campaign was involved in recruiting retired teacher Daniel J Sullivan to challenge Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.The Justice Department's lawsuit, which Trump said he had directed the department to file, sought to halt certification of the results and order an investigation if the victory margin indicated that voter confusion could have affected the outcome.However, US District Judge Sharon Gleason in Anchorage dismissed the case on Sunday, saying Alaska could not conduct such an investigation while maintaining the secrecy of ballots.Legal experts had questioned whether the Justice Department had the authority to pursue the case, warning that the move could create the impression that the federal government was favouring the Republican incumbent.Peter Keisler, who served as acting attorney general under former Republican President George W Bush, said the department needed to maintain political neutrality to retain public trust."For the department to be trusted in its law enforcement decisions it has to ensure that people understand it does not take sides in political partisan disputes," Keisler told Reuters.He added that the Alaska case had not only created the appearance of political interference but also represented an evident instance of taking sides.Blanche has defended the lawsuit, alleging that Daniel J Sullivan was involved in an attempt to mislead voters. The candidate has denied trying to confuse voters, while Peltola's campaign said it had "no involvement with either Sullivan campaign".Responding to criticism, a Justice Department official said during a press briefing on Thursday that the department filed lawsuits to enforce federal law.Trump allies gain greater control over election investigationsThe Justice Department has traditionally exercised caution in election-related investigations because federal intervention can create uncertainty and potentially be used by political candidates to challenge results.Its Public Integrity Section, which has career officials specialising in election law, previously advised investigators and prosecutors to wait until election results were certified before taking action, according to former department officials cited by Reuters.However, the Trump administration has reduced the size of the unit and suspended a requirement that federal prosecutors consult it during investigations into election-related corruption.Justice Department officials have argued that individual US attorney's offices are better placed to determine whether criminal charges should be pursued.According to three people familiar with internal discussions, agents and prosecutors have instead been told that political appointees of the Trump administration will decide unresolved disputes.The Deputy Attorney General's Office is also expected to mediate disagreements between investigators and prosecutors, a role former Justice Department officials said it has rarely played in election investigations.Pels defended the arrangement, saying resolving disputes that cannot be settled at the local level was precisely the purpose of the office.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'America taking its place': Shehbaz's rival Fazlur Rehman accuses Asim Munir of sabotaging ties with China
articles.summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Monday accused Pakistan army of derailing Chinese investments under the China-Pakistan
articles.body: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman on Monday accused Pakistan army of derailing Chinese investments under the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), alleging that the country's mineral wealth was being used to advance foreign interests and facilitate a shift towards United States.In a social media post on X, Rehman claimed that Pakistan had disappointed Beijing by halting CPEC-linked investments midway and warned that the loss of Chinese confidence could deter other countries from investing in Pakistan."You have disappointed China, you have halted their investment midway, and when China is disappointed, the rest of the world will not come to invest in your country either," he saidHe alleged that the US was stepping in to fill the space left by China, claiming that American officials had acknowledged this to him."And who is taking China's place? America is taking its place. This has been admitted by the Americans themselves in front of me," he said.Rehman clarified that he was not opposed to foreign investment in Pakistan's mineral sector, saying the country urgently needed international capital, development projects and economic opportunities."We do not disagree with the principle of investment from around the world here. Multinational companies come, they invest; America is not immune to this, Russia is not immune, China is not immune, Britain and France are not immune," he said."And who is taking China's place? America is taking its place. This has been admitted by the Americans themselves in front of me, and our esteemed elders here have taken those beautiful, beautiful stones to their offices and presented them, and the ambassador they have here at the time has also said it in her interview," he added.The JUI-F chief also alleged that politicians backed by the military establishment prioritised their personal interests and the demands of their patrons over Pakistan's economic well-being."These Pakistani politicians - whose priorities I know - in all such matters, they first determine their own share, and only then do they think about the country," he said.Fazlur Rehman also questioned the imposition of governor's rule and the declaration of an emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, alleging that the measures were linked to concerns over the region's mineral reserves."On what grounds? Terrorism? The provincial government is aligned with the narrative of terrorism; it is the federation that is not providing support for that narrative," he said.He further alleged that the focus on terrorism had subsequently disappeared from the debate, while discussions surrounding mineral reserves had also been dropped."As soon as governor's rule was imposed and as soon as the emergency was declared, the topic of terrorism simply vanished, and from their side, the discussion of mineral reserves was dropped," he said.His remarks come amid Pakistan's efforts to attract foreign investment into its mineral sector, particularly in resource-rich regions such as Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.CPEC, a flagship component of China's Belt and Road Initiative, includes infrastructure, energy and industrial development projects. The initiative has faced challenges over the years, including security threats, delays and concerns over the safety of Chinese personnel and investments.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meet Yip Ward and Paul Mappley, couple who couldn't afford a UK home buy French hamlet for £26,000, with seven cottages, two barns and more; save over £100,000 by renovating themselves
articles.summary: Yip Ward and Paul Mappley were living in a caravan in England when an unexpected opportunity changed their lives.
articles.body: Yip Ward and Paul Mappley were living in a caravan in England when an unexpected opportunity changed their lives. The couple bought an abandoned hamlet in Normandy, France, and have since taken on the mammoth task of restoring it themselves. Six years later, they own seven cottages, two barns and several other buildings, and estimate they have saved more than £100,000 through their DIY efforts.A couple who struggled to afford a home in the UK have turned an abandoned French hamlet into their dream property after purchasing it for just £26,000. Yip Ward and Paul Mappley, both 52, were living in a caravan in Tunbridge Wells when a friend offered them an opportunity to buy a property in Normandy in 2020. According to a report by the Daily Mail, the couple initially purchased the hamlet for £12,000, funding the deal by selling an old tractor and other possessions. They subsequently acquired the neighbouring buildings for another £14,000.Their estate, called La Busliere, now comprises seven cottages, two barns, a workshop, a cider press, two traditional bread ovens and several other outbuildings.The couple began restoring the property building by building and have already converted the original cottage into a holiday rental. A horsebox they brought from the UK has also been transformed into accommodation and has reportedly proved extremely popular with visitors.The report, based on conversations with the couple, reveals that they have saved more than £100,000 by undertaking much of the restoration work themselves, with assistance from their builder friend Ian, 62. They are now hoping to complete their second cottage by summer 2027.Yip and Paul first met at 15 before reuniting 13 years laterWhile their decision to buy an abandoned French hamlet might appear like an unexpected adventure, Yip and Paul's official website reveals that their story together began decades earlier.The couple first met at school when they were just 15 years old. However, life took them in different directions, and they lost touch for the next 13 years. They reunited in 2004, when they were in their late twenties, and that chance meeting became a turning point in both their lives.According to their website, their reunion inspired them to leave their previous lives behind and start afresh together. They initially had very little money and spent the following years trying different jobs, business ideas and moving homes as they worked towards building a stable future.Eventually, they found themselves living in a static mobile home on a friend's farm while building a landscaping business from scratch.Their website describes this period as one of determination and several fresh starts, with the couple gradually establishing themselves before the opportunity to move to France presented itself.How an £8,000 cottage turned into an entire French hamletThe couple's move to France was not part of a long-term plan. According to their official website, they first heard about a small house for sale in rural France for just £8,000.They worked hard, saved the money and purchased the property, initially without any intention of completely changing their lives.However, the cottage was located within a largely abandoned hamlet. What started as the purchase of one house soon developed into an opportunity to acquire the surrounding buildings.Their official website's FAQ gives the original purchase price as €10,000 in 2019. It also explains that by 2020, they had gone from owning one cottage to acquiring the majority of the abandoned hamlet. The remaining properties were purchased later, while they were filming their television series.Recalling how the unexpected opportunity came about, Yip told the Daily Mail, "People always say how did you find the village and it's not that we were looking, it was a chance meeting with a friend who had got a place and was selling it.""We definitely see it as the planets aligned. We went and sought out a wreck that had been abandoned 30 years ago and pieced it together," she added.At the time, the original sellers had reportedly reconsidered their decision because of the enormous amount of restoration work required. However, Yip and Paul were willing to take on the challenge.They continued working as landscape gardeners to fund the purchase. The couple also benefited from French payment arrangements that allowed them eight months before they had to hand over the entire sum.Looking back at how far they have come, Yip said, "We're really cracking on now. We say to ourselves we can't believe this whole place is ours.""Coming from where we come from I don't think the gratitude for being here will ever run out. It blows my mind," she added.Couple save more than £100,000 by renovating the cottages themselvesBuying the hamlet was only the beginning. The couple soon discovered the scale of the work required to bring the neglected buildings back to life.Several cottages had been almost completely taken over by nature, with thick ivy covering their roofs and walls. Some structures needed extensive repairs, while others required major restoration work.Speaking to the Daily Mail, Paul said, "I can't express to you enough that apart from cottages one and two, the other three cottages were covered, the whole roof in ivy.""They were literally being swallowed by nature. We're saving so much money doing it ourselves," he added.Rather than relying entirely on professional contractors, Yip and Paul decided to undertake much of the restoration themselves. They have already converted the original cottage into a holiday rental and also introduced a horsebox accommodation unit brought over from the UK.The couple are now working towards completing their second cottage by summer 2027.One of their biggest sources of support has been their friend Ian, 62, who has 47 years of experience in building restoration. He initially carried out repairs at their first cottage in 2019 but later reconnected with the couple after following their renovation journey on YouTube.Paul recalled how Ian came to their rescue when they were struggling to remove a massive rotten roof beam and had neither the money nor the machinery to complete the job."We had a massive two-ton roof thing that needed to come out as it was rotten on one end. We didn't have anyone, machinery or money and we were sharing on YouTube saying 'we don't know what to do'," he told the publication."He saw this video and arrived one day and said 'come on boys let's get this beam out'. For the first six months he worked for no payment."The couple are now able to pay Ian £1,000 a week through the income generated by their YouTube channel.Social media followers and locals help fund their restoration projectTheir restoration journey has also attracted considerable support from people who have followed their progress online.Paul revealed that people regularly turn up at the hamlet with donations, ranging from furniture to construction materials."We have five people turning up every single day to donate things – they bring bits of furniture or materials for the roof," he said."I can't tell you what a community we've built somehow. Every week we're donated £400 worth of materials for free we can use."The donations, combined with their willingness to undertake much of the work themselves, have helped them significantly reduce renovation costs.Paul cited the example of one section of the roof on their third cottage. While professional builders had quoted them £13,000 for the repairs, the couple managed to complete the work for just £2,000."We saved £11,000 just on one side of a roof. Take that per cottage doing it ourselves that's £22,000 per cottage, seven cottages which is instantly saving us over £100,000," he explained.The couple's journey has also been documented on Channel 4's Help! We Bought a Village. According to their official website, filming at La Busliere began in 2021, and their restoration work has since attracted viewers from around the world.Why the couple don't want to turn their French hamlet into a holiday rental businessWhile owning seven cottages could offer the couple an opportunity to build a lucrative holiday rental business, they have no intention of turning the entire hamlet into a commercial venture.Their ultimate plan is to live there permanently while retaining the peaceful atmosphere that attracted them to the property.Yip said that although people often tell them they could make substantial money by renting out all seven cottages, that is not what they envision for the future."People say 'once all seven cottages are done you'll rake it in'. We don't want it to be a metropolis," she told the Daily Mail.She explained that the absence of light pollution and the tranquillity of the location are among its biggest attractions. The couple want visitors to experience the same atmosphere rather than overcrowd the hamlet with holidaymakers.Instead, they plan to convert some of the remaining buildings into workshops and community spaces. They also hope to organise summer fairs, local markets, outdoor cinema screenings and pizza-making events using the property's two traditional ovens.The couple are equally keen to preserve the buildings' traditional character, avoiding modern additions such as televisions and UPVC windows in the cottages."There won't be things like TV's in the cottages. There won't be any UPVC windows," Yip said."It's an exciting, amazing place and we want to make sure people are transported back."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
